tools.name: comment

tools.description: Run one caller-authored Frida script against an explicitly selected process and detach when the observation window ends. tools.name: list_adb_devices

tools.name: list_adb_directory
tools.description: List the immediate children of one absolute device directory, including hidden entries: names, kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, dates, and symlink targets. tools.name: list_adb_features
tools.description: List the device's declared hardware and software features (`pm list features`) for device fingerprinting. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_packages
tools.description: List installed packages on one device with each base APK's device path, optionally scoped to third-party or system packages. Paths are device filesystem paths, not host-local. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_processes
tools.description: List running processes exactly as `ps -A` reports them: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, and name. Useful for pairing with instrumentation lanes. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_services
tools.description: List the device's binder services with their interfaces (`service list`). Read-only.

tools.name: list_bookmarks
tools.description: List every bookmark in the selected Hopper document as address and name pairs; unnamed bookmarks retain a null name. Use bookmarks as analyst-authored navigation aids; this does not discover code references.

tools.name: list_frida_devices
tools.description: List Frida devices currently available to this host, optionally connecting to the caller-selected remote Frida endpoint. Remote authentication options are used for this call only and are never returned or recorded.

tools.description: List every eligible Node/Electron V8 Inspector target from an explicit literal-loopback endpoint. Node discovery file locations that cannot be verified are preserved as unresolved reported URLs; they do not prove filesystem identity. Listing does not attach to targets.

tools.name: list_jeb_units

tools.name: list_names

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.description: List every analyzed procedure as address/value pairs after provider analysis. Ghidra metadata distinguishes thunks and external functions; use returned addresses in later function operations. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: List segments or memory blocks using exclusive end addresses. Ghidra reports block permissions, address space, image base, initialization, and overlay facts; Hopper marks unavailable permissions explicitly.

tools.name: list_strings

tools.description: Find installed packages by case-insensitive substring of the package name (e.g. `whatsapp` → `com.whatsapp`), returning each match's base APK device path. The first step of an easy get: resolve, then pull_adb_package the exact name. Read-only.

tools.name: resolve_containing_procedure
tools.description: Resolve an arbitrary address, including an interior instruction or exact external entry, to its provider-analyzed containing procedure. A negative result distinguishes outside segments from not in a procedure and is never guessed from nearby symbols.

tools.name: resolve_native_call_targets
tools.description: Resolve one explicit static call site using typed provider call references. Preserves ambiguous targets as candidates and unresolved computed calls as unknown; does not execute code or traverse a call graph.

tools.name: resume_frida_session
tools.description: Resume the process created by a paused Frida spawn session. Attached processes are already running and cannot be resumed through this operation.

tools.name: rizin_debug_command
tools.description: Execute one unrestricted command in a persistent Rizin debugger session. Returns raw output inline with Evidence, including backend output interleaved before the completion marker. If the command exceeds the output-byte, frame-byte, or frame-count limit, `output_truncated` is true and `completion_status` is `unknown`; retained partial output is returned and the owned debugger session is stopped. tools.name: rizin_debug_session_status
tools.description: Return observed lifecycle state and bounded recent NUL-framed output and process diagnostics for one Rizin debugger session; truncation fields report discarded data, and output_invalid_utf8 reports whether invalid UTF-8 has been observed in session frame bytes; recent output may contain replacement characters.

tools.name: search_android_classes
tools.description: Search complete top-level decompiler class-name rows in an explicit local APK by case-sensitive substring. Empty query inventories all rows. Repeated names remain repeated and appear in duplicate_names; the provider accepts only class names for lookup, so these rows do not identify which same-name class node a later lookup selects. Retains artifact and engine identity; no APK execution.

tools.name: search_bytes
tools.description: Find masked byte signatures in initialized analyzed memory. Hex byte pairs and ?? wildcards are supported; an optional equal-length hex mask selects bits. Bounds are inclusive. Matches are ordered by provider address and never span blocks. Coverage describes this page; reuse the same query with next_cursor to continue. Uninitialized blocks are listed separately. Ghidra only; Hopper is unavailable.

tools.name: search_procedures
tools.description: Search every analyzed procedure name using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker. tools.name: search_strings
tools.description: Search every provider-reported string object or candidate using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete over that provider inventory, not every text sequence in artifact bytes. Kuna scans mapped sequences of at least five characters, including unterminated fragments, without computing references. Ghidra may omit packed or undefined literals, incl

tools.name: set_address_name
tools.description: Assign an analyst name to one mapped hexadecimal address and report whether the native edit succeeded and exact readback matched. Hopper rejects symbol names exceeding 1024 UTF-16 code units before mutation, and rejects names owned by another address; use set_addresses_names to explicitly move or swap labels among selected addresses. This mutates analysis metadata.

tools.name: set_addresses_names
tools.description: Assign analyst names to multiple mapped addresses in one call and return per-address edit/readback success booleans. Hopper validates mapped destinations, native string representations, its 1024 UTF-16 code-unit symbol-name limit, and unique destinations/names before applying edits. Existing labels may move or swap only among explicitly selected addresses; unselected label owners remain unchanged.

tools.name: set_bookmark
tools.description: Create or update a bookmark at a mapped hexadecimal address and report readback success. Omit name to preserve an existing name or create an unnamed bookmark; an empty string clears the bookmark name. This mutates navigation metadata; bookmarks are analyst-authored navigation aids, not binary evidence.

tools.name: set_comment
tools.description: Write a regular analysis comment at a hexadecimal address and return whether readback matched. An empty comment clears it. This mutates the Hopper document; use comments to record evidence IDs or reasoning.

tools.name: set_inline_comment
tools.description: Write an inline instruction comment at a hexadecimal address and return whether readback matched. An empty comment clears it; Hopper may flatten newlines, producing false on exact readback. This mutates analysis metadata.

tools.name: start_adb_activity
tools.description: Start an intent with `am start -W`: one action, optional data URI, optional explicit component, and up to 16 typed extras (string, boolean, int, long, float). A device-mutating tool; the full wait report determines success, with failed-attempt facts and raw output retained.

tools.name: start_adb_app
tools.description: Start one installed app's resolved launcher activity with `am start -W -n`. A device-mutating tool for dynamic analysis. The full wait report determines success; failures retain launch-attempt facts and raw output. Pair with `read_adb_logcat` (pid filter) and `list_adb_processes` to observe the app, and `stop_adb_app` to end the run.

tools.name: start_frida_session
tools.description: Attach Frida to one selected process or spawn one selected target. Spawned targets remain paused until resume_frida_session, allowing scripts to load before execution. Closing a session detaches instrumentation; it does not kill the target.

tools.name: start_gdb_session
tools.description: Start a BYO GDB process in MI3 mode when available, suppress startup files, and disable auto-loading. tools.name: start_rizin_debug_session
tools.description: Start a persistent Rizin debugger session using `-N` to suppress user settings and scripts while retaining plugins, `-0` for NUL framing, and `-d` with an optional caller-selected IO debugger backend. Requires a caller-selected Linux TTY for inferior stdout and stderr; the target may write directly to that terminal while running and after detach. REA verifies both destinations and `dbg.exitkills=f

tools.name: stop_adb_app
tools.description: Force-stop every process of one package (`am force-stop`), ending a dynamic-analysis run. A device-mutating tool; it succeeds whether or not the package had running processes.

tools.name: trace_android_references
tools.description: Trace incoming static using nodes to an exact Android class or selected method overload. The total counts containing nodes, not individual invoke instructions. Use inspect_android_class to choose an overload_index when names collide. tools.name: trace_application_feature

Original static, native, passive-runtime, inferred, and unknown authorities remain distinct; native addon handoffs never open a provider or execute the application.

tools.name: trace_call_path
tools.description: Resolve start and optional goal symbols or addresses to canonical procedure entries, then trace direct callers or callees until the graph is exhausted or the goal is reached. tools.name: trace_feature
tools.description: Trace the complete literal query, preserving spaces, through every matching string and procedure, their xrefs, and truthful containing-procedure resolution. Returns observations and residual unknowns without inferring reference kinds.

tools.name: trace_javascript_semantics
tools.description: Trace static JavaScript data-flow, direct call/return, and closure relations from inline application Evidence or an exact same-session retained reference. Dynamic or unsupported semantics remain explicit unknowns; static reachability never claims runtime execution.

tools.name: trace_native_ui_action
tools.description: Trace one unique compiled UI action, object ID, native symbol or exact function address through authored connections, encoded or symbolized Objective-C handlers, and bounded static call references. Typed direct and resolved indirect calls, ambiguous candidates, inferred untyped provider callees, and targetless sites remain distinct. Runtime reachability is unknown; use trace_native_values for reco

tools.name: trace_native_values
tools.description: Trace a bounded static dependency graph from one explicit native procedure. Includes high-p-code def-use, constants, operators, memory and branch operations, resolved call edges, and derived argument/parameter and return/output bindings. Missing bindings, alias semantics, persistent state and RNG roles remain unknown. Budgets bound depth, decompilations, graph size and payloads; nodes are paginate

Reads a local export_web_scripts manifest and verifies the selected source's SHA-256/size; returns source positions, native resolved URLs or exact errors, every matching captured candidate and explicit unknown execution. tools.description: Trace one generated position in an exported website script through an explicitly paired local source map. tools.name: uninstall_adb_package
tools.description: Request package removal for user 0 (`adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`) without data retention. A device-mutating tool; absent packages report the device's own refusal reason.

tools.name: unload_frida_script
tools.description: Unload one caller-selected Frida script from a live session. This removes that script's instrumentation from the target.

tools.name: unset_bookmark
tools.description: Remove the bookmark at a mapped hexadecimal address and return whether it is absent. Hopper also permits removing an existing legacy bookmark outside mapped memory. This mutates navigation metadata and does not alter binary bytes.

tools.name: update_analysis_settings
tools.description: When REA names an adjustable limit, atomically set or reset its runtime default, then retry once work and cleanup have settled. No inspection call is required when the error supplies the bounds. Changes apply only to new work, survive target close/open, and disappear on REA restart. Reset restores launch configuration. Does not edit files, restart providers, raise host limits, or override explicit

tools.name: update_unknown
tools.description: Append one immutable full-state revision and mutation evidence. Requires exact expected_revision; stale concurrent writers fail instead of overwriting newer analysis.

tools.name: verify_managed_native_boundaries
tools.description: Verify managed P/Invoke/native-boundary declarations against authenticated native export or function Evidence without executing managed code or translating managed metadata tokens into native addresses. The workflow preserves declaration-only, verified, inferred, contradicted, and unresolved states; a name candidate with missing managed or native module identity remains unresolved with its candida

tools.name: verify_reconstruction
tools.description: Verify a finite typed behavioral and structural specification against a canonical Evidence bundle. Pass means every declared claim has complete comparable authority—not global source equivalence; changed claims fail and missing, limited, or unresolved evidence stays unknown.

tools.name: verify_unknown_resolution
tools.description: Revalidate the current residual-unknown head against live bundled evidence, exact authority/confidence/environment requirements, and revision integrity. Withdrawn and out-of-scope dispositions are not truth claims.

tools.name: xrefs
tools.description: Return analyzed references to a code or data address. Hopper may default to its current cursor; headless providers such as Ghidra require an explicit address. Use to connect strings, globals, selectors, and functions; bare addresses are untyped and indirect references may be incomplete. Use inspect_native_instruction at the target address for typed incoming references where supported.
